Prevention: Adequate fertilization and watering improves resilience to attack
Grow tolerant variety of citrus and conserve natural enemies, e.g. parasitoid wasps.
Monitoring: Regularly visit field and look for silvery zig-zag mines and curled leaves on citrus plants, especially the young tender leaves
Extensively mined leaves may be deformed and distorted, irregularly curled in shape, pale in colour, or defective in function, and may dry up and fall off
Growth of young plants is retarded and seedlings may even die
Observe neighboring host plants for similar symptoms
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Pruning and destruction of heavily infested leaves showing curled and zig- zag mining symptoms during winter
Citrus leaf miner moths are attracted to the new flush of citrus trees.
Avoid pruning live branches more than once a year, so that the cycles of flushing are uniform and short
Direct Control (Chemical): BARI Wash hands and clothes after insecticide spray
Don't drink and smoke during spraying
Both contact and systemic insecticides can be used to control leafminer caterpillars
Thiamethoxam, usually @ 0.5 g / L of water at 15 day intervals
